title: Orsen and the Wolf
premise: Wendell Zhou, a mercenary bound by oath to Orsen, a mountain god who fell silent thirteen years ago, has survived by staying invisible—smuggling goods, never prayers. But when the old gods suddenly begin answering again, Wendell discovers their silence was not abandonment but imprisonment, and that they themselves are the unwitting vessel of the secret: the location of Orsen's stolen heart. Hunted by the resurgent church of the new gods and shadowed by a wolf that may be Orsen's last living servant, Wendell must choose between returning the heart—reigniting the ancient war between old and new gods—or destroying it and severing every divine power in Thornfell forever, including their own patron's survival. In the end, Wendell gives the heart to the wolf, who is revealed to be Orsen reborn mortal, choosing loyalty to a person over truth to a god, and letting the war die unlit as the thirteenth moon sets.
about_author: Oscar Okonkwo is a former cartographer who spent six years mapping trade routes through remote highland regions before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy rooted in the geography of belief, where mountains remember what people forget.

chapters.title: The Silent Altar
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. On a smuggling run through Thornfell, Wendell passes the ruined altar where they once swore their oath to Orsen, now choked with moss. A prayer slips out unbidden—and something answers for the first time in thirteen years. Emotional beat: unease; the safety of silence is broken.

chapters.title: Salt and Silver
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. In the border town of Greyhollow, Wendell delivers contraband salt and learns the new gods' church is posting rewards for anyone who 'hears voices.' Their handler, Maren, warns them to stop praying. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; Wendell realizes the answer was heard by more than them.

chapters.title: The Wolf on the Pass
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A huge grey wolf begins trailing Wendell through the high passes—not hunting, watching. When bandits ambush Wendell at Kestrel Notch, the wolf intervenes with uncanny intelligence. Emotional beat: reluctant wonder; Wendell cannot decide if this is omen or threat.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Wendell, with an interlude of the wolf's senses. Sheltering in a cave shrine, Wendell dreams Orsen's memories: a theft, a buried heart, a betrayal by fellow gods. They wake with knowledge they never asked for. Emotional beat: dread; invisibility is officially over.

chapters.title: Maren's Price
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Maren reveals she sold word of Wendell's 'answering' to the church to cover her own debts, and begs forgiveness even as she hands them over. Wendell escapes Greyhollow through the smugglers' tunnels only they know. Emotional beat: bitter betrayal; loyalty has a market price.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Vael
chapters.summary: POV Inquisitor Sera Vael. The church's chief hunter interrogates Maren and reconstructs Wendell's route from toll records. Vael is no zealot—she believes ending the old gods will end the war before it starts. Emotional beat: cold resolve; the antagonist is given a sympathetic spine.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. An oracle in a drowned chapel explains the clock: when the thirteenth moon completes its turn, the seal on Orsen's prison breaks whether or not the heart is found. Wendell learns the heart's location is locked inside their own memory. Emotional beat: trapped; the deadline becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Company That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell seeks their old mercenary company, sworn like them to Orsen, hoping allies share the burden. Most are dead or renounced; one, Brannic, agrees to help—for a promise of the heart's power. Emotional beat: hollow reunion; shared oaths do not mean shared loyalties.

chapters.title: Hunted Through Thornfell
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wendell and Vael. A running chase across three chapters of mountain: Vael's riders close in, Brannic's judgment wavers, and the wolf repeatedly saves Wendell at escalating cost. Emotional beat: exhaustion and growing trust between Wendell and the wolf.

chapters.title: Blood Oath
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Cornered at the Weeping Stair, Wendell binds themselves formally to the wolf with old-rite blood, naming it companion rather than beast. The bond floods them with Orsen's pain. Emotional beat: commitment; Wendell stops being a bystander to the gods' war.

chapters.title: The Heart Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Following dream-memory, they reach the sealed vault under Mount Ceren where Orsen's heart lies in chains of prayer-iron. Brannic turns on them here, wanting the heart's power for himself. Emotional beat: confrontation; greed dressed as faith.

chapters.title: Brannic's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Brannic. Holding the freed heart, Brannic feels its hunger and understands why the gods went to war over it. He nearly uses it, then falters—and Vael's crossbow bolt finds him. Emotional beat: tragedy; the corrupted seek power and are destroyed by it.

chapters.title: Ash and Iron
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. With the heart loose and Vael arriving with her full company, the vault battle erupts. The heart's raw divinity scorches everyone near it; Wendell barely escapes with it wrapped in their oath-cloak. Emotional beat: chaos; power corrupts everything it touches.

chapters.title: Vael's Mercy
chapters.summary: POV Vael. Vael captures Wendell but hesitates to kill—the heart whispers to her too, offering restoration of her dead sister. She recognizes the corruption beginning in herself. Emotional beat: crisis of conscience inside the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Prisoner's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. In the church stockade, Wendell offers Vael a third path: destroy the heart entirely, ending all divine power in Thornfell—including the church's miracles. Vael must weigh her faith against her fear. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance across enemy lines.

chapters.title: Escape from Greyhollow
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wendell and Vael. The two break out together as the thirteenth moon wanes and the seal weakens—earthquakes, answered prayers gone wrong, shrines bleeding light. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; the world itself is fraying.

chapters.title: Where the Wolf Sleeps
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The wolf leads them to a hidden den above the cloudline and finally speaks—with Orsen's voice. It is the god, reduced to flesh, having sent its heart away to survive. Emotional beat: revelation; the loyal servant was the god all along.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Orsen asks for its heart back, promising to win the coming war and reward Wendell beyond measure. Wendell sees the corruption already reshaping the god's mind and refuses, proposing instead that the heart be destroyed. Emotional beat: heartbreak; love means saying no.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV Wendell and Vael. At the summit shrine as the final moon rises, the seal breaks fully and the old gods stir toward war. Wendell, Vael, and the wolf hold the heart at the altar while divine forces converge. Emotional beat: climax pressure; everything converges on one choice.

chapters.title: Unmaking
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell drives the oath-blade through the heart, unmaking it—and with it all divine power in Thornfell. The converging gods collapse into silence mid-stride; the war dies unborn. Wendell's own oath-marks burn away. Emotional beat: sacrifice; the price of survival is paid in full.

chapters.title: A God Made Mortal
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Freed of divinity, the wolf remains—a mortal creature with Orsen's memory but none of its hunger. Wendell chooses to stay with it rather than return to the roads. Emotional beat: quiet tenderness; what survives the fire is small and enough.

chapters.title: The Road Without Gods
chapters.summary: POV Wendell, epilogue. A year later, Wendell walks the smuggler's roads openly, guiding travelers through a Thornfell where prayers go unanswered and people must answer each other. Vael sends word of a fragile peace. Emotional beat: resolution; loyalty outlived the truth it served.
